title: Relations as a module over the target prime field
name: 01-relation-module
notes: A retraction onto the cyclic order-n component is an explicit hypothesis; such a retraction does not exist for every subgroup of an arbitrary finite abelian group. If #G=hn with gcd(h,n)=1, [h] followed by the inverse of h modulo n supplies one. For the ECCp-131 cover, f* composed with [2 inverse modulo n] and f_* supplies a retraction onto the embedded elliptic group. The matrix columns are logarithms of projected factor-base elements. A usable left-kernel vector must have nonzero pairing with b; a raw count of relations does not certify this.

title: Divisor smoothness: factorization and support
name: 02-divisor-smoothness
notes: This page uses an odd-degree imaginary model with one rational point at infinity. The factorization formula is displayed for squarefree u. The probability is a counting heuristic, not a universal theorem for structured factor bases or an embedded elliptic subgroup. B counts the signed set of admissible degree-one classes; quotienting by the involution changes the bookkeeping. In the small-genus large-prime variation, the exceptional primes here are degree-one places outside the chosen factor base.

title: Summation polynomials and Weil restriction
name: 03-summation-weil
notes: Semaev polynomials characterize geometric point-sum relations. Each variable of S_(m+1) has degree 2^(m−1). For x_i in the base field, coefficient expansion over a degree-d extension gives d equations; independence is an additional condition. The fixed-d Gaudry cost is a heuristic algorithmic regime, not an unconditional bound for every curve, target specialization, or factor base. For a,b,x_R and x_i all in the base field, the other coefficient equations vanish identically. This statement does not cover arbitrary nonrational affine x-lines.

title: Covers, norm maps and elliptic factors
name: 04-covers-prym
notes: For C2 the other elliptic quotient is u=X^(−2), v=Y/X^3, with equation v²=b u³+a u²+1. The two quotient maps give a (2,2)-split Jacobian. The sextic has two rational infinity points, so the fiber divisor uses infinity_+ + infinity_- as reference. A general even-degree reduced-divisor convention needs care. For C3, the projective equation W^4=X^3 Z+aXZ^3+bZ^4 is smooth when the elliptic cubic is squarefree and the characteristic exceeds 3; its degree-two cover has an abelian-surface Prym. The norm–pullback identity proves injectivity on odd-order torsion, without implying that the full Jacobian is cyclic.

title: Frobenius decomposes the extension-field groups
name: 05-frobenius-components
notes: For ECCp-131 the full quadratic group is odd and decomposes into the +1 and −1 eigenspaces, identified with the curve and its quadratic twist over Fp. For the cubic group, T3 is surjective onto E(Fp), since multiplication by 3 is invertible there; rho3 is its normalized retraction. The verified coprimality also separates the target prime from ker T3. Infinity is excluded from the literal x-coordinate factor base on the cubic side. Nonrational affine x-lines produce other factor bases; projecting their relations remains valid but does not prove a universal algorithmic lower bound.

title: Complexity regimes: ambient group or target subgroup?
name: 06-complexity-regimes
notes: The default chart holds the embedded target order n≈q fixed while retaining the original field; its rho cost is sqrt(n), even in a larger Jacobian. The displayed IC bars in that mode are ambient benchmarks, marked with a dagger: their model/class-group and relation-statistics assumptions do not automatically hold for split covers. The equal-field mode instead assumes a large generic subgroup of order about q^g. The equal-group mode compares independently parameterized generic groups of order N, using q≈N^(1/g); it does not describe the covers of ECCp-131. Hyperelliptic q^(2−2/g) statements require fixed genus and the hypotheses of the selected theorem/algorithm, including cyclic class-group assumptions in the cited rigorous result. The plane-quartic O-tilde(q) result uses its own geometric conditions. These are upper-bound regimes, not lower bounds or measured runtimes.

title: Worked extraction: three rows can determine k—or fail
name: 07-worked-kernel
notes: This is a constructed toy example, not harvested attack data. The curve over F571 is the coefficient reduction of the challenge curve; its order is 557. Q=[37]P and the chosen factor-base points are [11]P and [23]P, used only to construct and verify the rows. In the usable mode, a=(494,469,332), b=(2,3,7), w=(-1,-1,1), w^Ta=483 and w^Tb=2. Changing a3 to 406 and b3 to 5 keeps all rows valid but makes both pairings zero; the augmented rank falls to 2, so these rows alone leave k free.

title: Partial relations: cancel the large-prime columns
name: 08-partial-relations
notes: The large-prime coefficient rows are (1,-1,0), (0,1,-1), and (-1,0,1), so their sum is zero. Signs matter: arbitrary relations with two exceptional terms do not automatically cancel around every unsigned cycle. The numerical check realizes the identities in the toy order-557 elliptic component with factor-base logs 11,23,31 and exceptional logs 5,9,14. It is an algebraic illustration of the recombination mechanism, not a claim that these data were collected in a hyperelliptic factor-base search. In the small-genus large-prime variation, the exceptional classes represented by the graph are degree-one places outside the selected factor base.

title: Fiber smoothness is a structured distribution
name: 09-fiber-census
notes: For the published ECCp-131 curve, the quadratic character of x_P is +1 and that of x_Q is −1. The Q fiber is nevertheless an Fp-rational degree-two divisor because Frobenius swaps its geometric points. The plot uses a different, explicitly labeled toy curve E/F571: y²=x³+508x+137, #E=557. Its genus-two companion quotient has order 609, hence #J=339213. The signed factor-base point set F_B is stable under the deck and hyperelliptic involutions, and excludes X=0 and infinity. Let S_B consist of classes of A+A'−D_infinity supported on F_B with distinct X. There are B(B−1)/2 unordered point pairs, of which B/2 share an X; hence |S_B|=B²/2−B. They give distinct classes because nonspecial degree-two divisors on a genus-two curve are unique in their linear-equivalence class; distinct X excludes the hyperelliptic pencil. Exactly B/2 nonidentity elliptic targets have their full fiber in F_B. Thus the two displayed probabilities have different sampling spaces and are exact in this toy setup. The E targets and support-pair encodings are enumerated; the whole Jacobian is not. These counts are not an attack-cost estimate. The final projection identity is for a split fiber over P, with the specified infinity reference.

title: From more roots to less total work
name: 10-cost-accounting
notes: The sliders are an illustrative phase-average model, not ECCp-131 measurements. Baseline A uses trial cost 1, verified-row probability 0.02, and effective information fraction 0.5, giving cost 100 per effective row. Alternative B initially has twice the verified-row yield but four times the trial cost, giving 200. Effective information is a modeling proxy encompassing rank/recombination; it is not automatically an independent Bernoulli success probability and may vary during collection. The sparse linear-algebra estimate describes a near-square filtered matrix and Wiedemann-style Krylov work, omitting algorithm-specific preconditioning, logarithmic factors, block strategies and dense-fill effects. Costs require a common calibrated work unit before comparison with rho or a different solver.
